# github.com/go-again/sqlite — Consumer guide

This file is for AI coding agents (and humans) integrating
`github.com/go-again/sqlite` as a dependency in another project. It
collects everything an outside caller needs that doesn't fit cleanly
into per-package `doc.go` comments: which driver name to pick, which
DSN flags work, when to reach for each sub-package, the pitfalls that
won't show up until runtime, and the migration recipes from the four
upstream packages this one replaces.

For maintainers working **inside** this repo, read `CLAUDE.md` /
`AGENTS.md` instead.

# What this package is

A pure-Go (CGo-free) SQLite driver that registers under both `"sqlite"`
(modernc-compatible) and `"sqlite3"` (mattn-compatible) — pick whichever
matches the import you're swapping in. Same singleton driver under both
names; no behavioural split. Built on `modernc.org/sqlite`'s transpiled
SQLite engine, with a hand-written wrapper that adds:

- The mattn-compat surface: `*SQLiteDriver` with `Extensions` and
  `ConnectHook` fields, `RegisterFunc` / `RegisterAggregator` on the
  driver, `ConnectionHook` API.
- Per-conn helpers absent upstream: `RegisterUpdateHook`,
  `RegisterAuthorizer`, `SetTrace`, `RegisterPreUpdateHook`, `Backup`,
  `Serialize` / `Deserialize`, `FileControl`, `GetLimit`/`SetLimit`,
  `LoadExtension` / `EnableLoadExtension`, the SESSION extension
  (`CreateSession` → `*Session`, `ApplyChangeset` with a Go conflict
  handler, `InvertChangeset` / `ConcatChangesets`) — no other pure-Go
  driver exposes changesets — plus introspection/telemetry
  (`TableColumnMetadata`, `Status` for sqlite3_db_status, `TxnState`,
  `(*Stmt).Readonly` / `Status`), WAL control (`WALCheckpoint` with
  returned frame counts, `WALAutoCheckpoint`, `RegisterWALHook`,
  `GetSnapshot` / `OpenSnapshot`), `SetProgressHandler`, `SetDBConfig`
  / `QueryDBConfig` (DEFENSIVE / TRUSTED_SCHEMA security flags), and
  R-Tree custom geometry/query callbacks (`RegisterRTreeGeometry` /
  `RegisterRTreeQuery`).
- Typed Go APIs for two extensions: **vec** (sqlite-vec, vector search)
  and **fts** (FTS5, full-text search). Both ship gorm bridges that wire
  the sidecar tables to gorm models via struct tags.
- A gorm dialector (a verbatim port of `glebarez/sqlite` rewired to use
  this driver).
- A `vfs` adapter that lets you back an `*sql.DB` with any `io/fs.FS` —
  `embed.FS`, `fstest.MapFS`, a zip-fs, anything.

The project supports the **two most recent Go releases**. The actual
pin lives in `go.mod`; when a new minor ships, the just-superseded
release drops out within one cycle. Modern syntax is treated as a
feature, not an accident: generics, `iter.Seq2`, `log/slog`, generic
type aliases, `range over int`, `sync.WaitGroup.Go`, `strings.SplitSeq`,
`reflect.TypeFor` are all in use. `just lint` runs `gopls modernize`
to keep new contributions on the leading idiom.

# Picking the driver name

Two names register the same `*Driver` singleton:

```go
import _ "github.com/go-again/sqlite"

db, _ := sql.Open("sqlite",  "file:app.db") // modernc name
db, _ := sql.Open("sqlite3", "file:app.db") // mattn name
```

Use whichever name the existing code uses. Switching name within a
project changes nothing; it's purely cosmetic. The `Driver{}` struct
literal (mattn's `&SQLiteDriver{Extensions: …, ConnectHook: …}`) is
available under both type aliases.

# Configuring the connection

There are two ways to configure a connection. Reach for the structured Go-typed `sqlite.Config` first; the DSN flags are documented for the compat surface and for callers integrating with DSN-only tools.

## Modern: sqlite.Config (Go-typed, recommended)

```go
import sqlite "github.com/go-again/sqlite"

db, err := sqlite.Open(sqlite.Config{
    Path:    "myapp.db",
    Pragmas: sqlite.RecommendedPragmas(), // WAL + busy_timeout=5s + foreign_keys
    MaxOpenConns: 8,
})
if err != nil { ... }
defer db.Close()
```

The returned `*sqlite.DB` embeds `*sql.DB`, so every `database/sql` method works unchanged. PRAGMAs ride in as DSN `_pragma=` URL flags under the hood — the driver applies them on every new connection in the pool, not just the one `database/sql` happens to pick for the first Exec. A single `defer db.Close()` drains the pool AND releases any encryption VFS the open registered.

The `Pragmas` struct: `JournalMode`, `BusyTimeout`, `Synchronous`, `ForeignKeys`, `CacheSize`, `TempStore`, plus `Extra map[string]string` as an escape hatch for everything else. Empty / zero fields are "leave SQLite at its default."

Encryption at rest uses the same Config shape:

```go
import "github.com/go-again/sqlite/vfs/crypto"

key, err := crypto.DeriveKey(passphrase, salt, sqlite.Adiantum) // Argon2id
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
db, _ := sqlite.Open(sqlite.Config{
    Path:    "secret.db",
    Pragmas: sqlite.RecommendedPragmas(),
    Encryption: &sqlite.Encryption{
        Key:    key,
        Cipher: sqlite.Adiantum, // or sqlite.AESXTS (64-byte key)
    },
})
```

For gorm, the same Config type via `sqlitegorm.OpenConfig`:

```go
import (
    sqlite     "github.com/go-again/sqlite"
    sqlitegorm "github.com/go-again/sqlite/gorm"
)

db, err := sqlitegorm.OpenConfig(sqlite.Config{
    Path:    "myapp.db",
    Pragmas: sqlite.RecommendedPragmas(),
})
defer db.Close()
db.AutoMigrate(&MyModel{}) // *gorm.DB methods, unchanged
```

Runnable end-to-end demos: [examples/sqlite-config](examples/sqlite-config/main.go) (plain `database/sql`) and [examples/gorm-config](examples/gorm-config/main.go) (gorm). The encrypted variants in both verify the on-disk file is opaque (SQLite header not visible).

## Escape hatches for legacy DSN callers

- `sqlite.BuildDSN(Config) string` renders the full DSN the modern entry would build, including `_pragma=` URL flags. Useful if you have a third-party tool that only takes a DSN string.
- `sqlite.ApplyPragmas(db *sql.DB, p Pragmas) error` applies the typed PRAGMAs to a pool you opened via the bare `sql.Open("sqlite", dsn)` path. Best-effort for per-connection PRAGMAs (the Exec only hits whichever idle conn the pool picks); for pool-wide correctness, use `sqlite.Open(Config)` instead.

## DSN flags

Accepted (subset of mattn's `_*` flags, translated to modernc's
parameter names):

- `cache=shared` / `cache=private`
- `mode=ro` / `mode=rw` / `mode=rwc` / `mode=memory`
- `_journal=WAL` (and the other journal modes)
- `_busy_timeout=N` (alias `_timeout`)
- `_foreign_keys=on`
- `_synchronous=NORMAL` (and FULL/OFF/EXTRA)
- `_case_sensitive_like=on`
- `_locking_mode=NORMAL` / `EXCLUSIVE`
- `_recursive_triggers=on`
- `_secure_delete=on`
- `_loc=Local` / `_loc=UTC` (time conversion)
- `_texttotime=1` — go-again-specific: scans DATETIME columns as
  `time.Time` instead of RFC3339 strings in map-mode reads. The gorm
  dialector injects this automatically. Set it manually if you want the
  same behaviour with raw `database/sql` map-row scans.
- `_stmt_cache_size=N` — sizes the per-connection prepared-statement
  LRU cache (default 100, 0 disables). Each conn in a pool holds its
  own cache capped at N, so aggregate memory scales with pool size.
  Inspect counters via `(*sqlite.Conn).StmtCacheStats()`.

Rejected with a clear error:

- `_auth*` (userauth, dropped by modernc upstream — not coming back).
- `_mutex=no` (modernc doesn't expose the unsafe single-threaded mode).

# Sub-package picker

Reach for the smallest sub-package that solves your problem.

## I just want SQL

```go
import sqlite "github.com/go-again/sqlite"

db, _ := sqlite.Open(sqlite.Config{
    Path:    "app.db",
    Pragmas: sqlite.RecommendedPragmas(),
})
defer db.Close()
```

Use `database/sql` methods on `db` as normal (it embeds `*sql.DB`). The legacy DSN form `sql.Open("sqlite", "file:app.db?_journal=WAL&_foreign_keys=on")` still works for callers who already wired it up.

## I want gorm

```go
import (
    sqlite     "github.com/go-again/sqlite"
    sqlitegorm "github.com/go-again/sqlite/gorm"
)

db, _ := sqlitegorm.OpenConfig(sqlite.Config{
    Path:    "app.db",
    Pragmas: sqlite.RecommendedPragmas(),
})
defer db.Close()
```

Use `*gorm.DB` methods on `db` as normal (it embeds the gorm DB). The legacy DSN form `gorm.Open(sqlitegorm.Open("file:app.db"), &gorm.Config{})` still works.

`sqlitegorm.Open` is a drop-in for `glebarez/sqlite.Open` and
`gorm.io/driver/sqlite.Open`. The dialector implements
`gorm.Dialector`, `gorm.Migrator`, `gorm.ErrorTranslator`, and
`gorm.SavePointerDialectorInterface`. AutoMigrate works, including the
ALTER-via-CREATE-INSERT-DROP-RENAME flow for column-type changes that
plain SQLite doesn't support.

## I want vector search

Raw API:

```go
import (
    _ "github.com/go-again/sqlite"
    _ "github.com/go-again/sqlite/vec"   // blank import: registers sqlite-vec on every conn
    "github.com/go-again/sqlite/vec"
)

tbl, _ := vec.Create(ctx, db, "docs", 384, vec.Options{Metric: vec.Cosine})
tbl.BatchInsert(ctx, []vec.Row{{Rowid: 1, Embedding: vector1}, ...})
for n, err := range tbl.KNN(ctx, query, 5, vec.WithFilter("rowid > ?", 100)) {
    if err != nil { return err }
    fmt.Println(n.Rowid, n.Distance)
}
```

With gorm (tag-driven sidecars):

```go
import (
    sqlitegorm "github.com/go-again/sqlite/gorm"
    vecgorm    "github.com/go-again/sqlite/vec/gorm"
)

type Document struct {
    ID        uint `gorm:"primaryKey"`
    Title     string
    Embedding vecgorm.Embedding `vec:"dim=384;metric=cosine"`
}

db, _ := gorm.Open(sqlitegorm.Open("file:app.db"), &gorm.Config{})
db.Use(vecgorm.Plugin())
vecgorm.Migrate(db, &Document{}) // creates documents + documents_vec sidecar
db.Create(&doc)                  // sidecar auto-syncs via AfterCreate
hits, _ := vecgorm.KNN[Document](ctx, db, query, 5)
```

## I want full-text search

Raw API:

```go
import (
    _ "github.com/go-again/sqlite"
    "github.com/go-again/sqlite/fts"
)

idx, _ := fts.New[int64, string](ctx, db, "docs", fts.Options{
    Tokenizer: fts.Porter{Base: fts.Unicode61{}},
})
idx.Insert(ctx, fts.Attr[int64, string]{Key: 1, Value: "the quick brown fox"})
hits, _ := idx.SearchSlice(ctx, fts.Term("fox"), fts.WithRanking())
```

With gorm:

```go
import ftsgorm "github.com/go-again/sqlite/fts/gorm"

type Article struct {
    ID    uint   `gorm:"primaryKey"`
    Title string `fts5:"tokenize=porter+unicode61"`
    Body  string `fts5:"tokenize=porter+unicode61"`
}

db.Use(ftsgorm.Plugin())
ftsgorm.Migrate(db, &Article{}) // creates articles_fts + AI/AU/AD triggers
hits, _ := ftsgorm.Search[Article](ctx, db, fts.Term("fox"))
```

Tag keys: `tokenize`, `prefix`, `external` (default `true`), `detail`,
`contentless` (default `false`), `table`. Three modes:
**external-content** (default; triggers sync from the source table),
**in-table** (`external=false`; FTS5 stores the text), **contentless**
(`contentless=true`; index-only, snippet/highlight unavailable).

## I want hybrid search (semantic + lexical)

```go
import "github.com/go-again/sqlite/fusion"

vecHits, _ := tbl.KNNSlice(ctx, queryVec, 50)
ftsHits, _ := idx.SearchSlice(ctx, fts.Term("brown fox"), fts.WithLimit(50))

vecKeys := make([]int64, len(vecHits))
for i, h := range vecHits { vecKeys[i] = h.Rowid }
ftsKeys := make([]int64, len(ftsHits))
for i, h := range ftsHits { ftsKeys[i] = h.Key }

top, err := fusion.RRF([][]int64{vecKeys, ftsKeys}, fusion.WithLimit(20))
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
```

Reciprocal Rank Fusion (Cormack 2009) — pure Go, no SQL, no extension. `fusion.WithK(k)` tunes the rank-1-vs-rank-N spread; `fusion.WithWeights(w1, w2, …)` lets a ranker you trust more dominate. Works over any comparable key type, not just SQLite rowids.

## I want a window function from Go

```go
sc, _ := db.Conn(ctx)
sc.Raw(func(dc any) error {
    c := dc.(*sqlite.Conn)
    return c.RegisterWindowFunction("running_sum", 1,
        func() sqlite.WindowAccumulator { return &sumState{} }, true)
})
```

`WindowAccumulator` is an interface with `Step` / `Inverse` / `Value`. Per-query state lives on the accumulator. Implement the optional `WindowFinalizer` interface (`Final`) only if you need per-instance cleanup. SQL works as usual: `SELECT running_sum(v) OVER (ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) FROM t`.

## I want to embed a SQLite file inside my binary

```go
import (
    "embed"
    _ "github.com/go-again/sqlite"
    "github.com/go-again/sqlite/vfs"
)

//go:embed seed.db
var seed embed.FS

func main() {
    name, _, _ := vfs.New(seed)
    db, _ := sql.Open("sqlite", "file:seed.db?vfs="+name+"&mode=ro")
}
```

Read-only by design (the `fs.FS` contract doesn't allow writes). Append
`&mode=ro` so SQLite rejects writes at open time with a clear error
rather than mid-query.

## I want loadable Go extensions (regexp, uuid, hash, stats, unicode, …)

The `ext/` umbrella ships opt-in SQL functions and vtab modules as Go-native ports of the ncruces/go-sqlite3 extension lineup. Each sub-package is independent; pick what you need and leave the rest off your import graph.

```go
import (
    sqlite "github.com/go-again/sqlite"
    _ "github.com/go-again/sqlite/ext/regexp/auto"    // REGEXP + regexp_*
    _ "github.com/go-again/sqlite/ext/uuid/auto"      // uuid() + gen_random_uuid + parse/format
    _ "github.com/go-again/sqlite/ext/hash/auto"      // md5/sha2/sha3/blake2/...
    _ "github.com/go-again/sqlite/ext/stats/auto"     // var_pop, percentile, regr_*, median, mode, ...
    _ "github.com/go-again/sqlite/ext/unicode/auto"   // upper/lower locale-aware, normalize, unaccent, collations
    _ "github.com/go-again/sqlite/ext/blobio/auto"    // readblob / writeblob over (*Conn).OpenBlob
    _ "github.com/go-again/sqlite/ext/closure/auto"   // transitive_closure graph walker
    _ "github.com/go-again/sqlite/ext/pivot/auto"     // three-SELECT cross-tab vtab
    _ "github.com/go-again/sqlite/ext/statement/auto" // parametrized-view vtab
    // _ "github.com/go-again/sqlite/ext/fileio/auto"    // os-backed read/write+fsdir — opt in only for trusted SQL
)
```

Each `<name>/auto` sub-package wires the extension via a `Driver.ConnectHook` so every new connection auto-registers. For per-connection control (or to bypass the auto's defaults), call `<name>.Register(c)` on a pinned `*sqlite.Conn` instead.

The full lineup:

- **`array`** — eponymous vtab that exposes a bound Go slice as a single-column SQL table. Two binding styles: transparent `db.Query("SELECT value FROM array(?)", sqlite.Pointer(slice))` (preferred — destructor releases on stmt finalize) or explicit `array.Bind(c, slice) → token, release()` for long-lived bindings.
- **`blobio`** — `readblob(schema, table, column, rowid, offset, n) → BLOB`, `writeblob(schema, table, column, rowid, offset, data) → INTEGER`, and `openblob(schema, table, column, rowid, write, callback, args...)` scalars over `(*Conn).OpenBlob`. `openblob` ferries a Go `blobio.OpenCallback` via `sqlite.Pointer` — the callback gets the live `*sqlite.Blob` handle plus trailing args, useful when one SQL invocation needs multiple Go-side operations on the same blob. For tight Go loops, call `(*Conn).OpenBlob` directly instead.
- **`bloom`** — persistent Bloom-filter vtab. `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE f USING bloom(size=10000, p=0.01)`, `INSERT INTO f(word) VALUES (?)`, then `SELECT present FROM f WHERE word = ?` to test membership. Bit array lives in a `<vtab>_storage` shadow blob via `(*Conn).OpenBlob`; survives `db.Close()` / reconnect. Stable cross-process Kirsch–Mitzenmacher hashing.
- **`closure`** — `transitive_closure` vtab. `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE temp.tc USING transitive_closure(tablename=org, idcolumn=id, parentcolumn=manager)`, then `SELECT id, depth FROM temp.tc WHERE root = 42 AND depth <= 3` to walk every descendant of node 42. Cycle-safe (visited-set), optional `depth = ?` / `<= ?` / `< ?` bounds. Schema args can also be supplied at query time via HIDDEN columns for multi-graph workloads.
- **`csv`** — vtab over RFC 4180 CSV files. `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE name USING csv(filename='x.csv', header=on, schema='CREATE TABLE x(a INTEGER, b TEXT)')` and then SELECT / JOIN / aggregate against it normally. `csv.Register(c)` uses `os.Open`; `csv.RegisterFS(c, fsys)` sandboxes file access to an `fs.FS` (embed.FS, fstest.MapFS, os.DirFS). Type affinity is inferred from the schema's INTEGER / REAL / TEXT keywords.
- **`fileio`** — `readfile(path) → BLOB`, `writefile(path, data [, mode]) → INTEGER`, `lsmode(mode_int) → TEXT`, plus the `fsdir(root [, depth])` recursive-walk vtab. `fileio.Register(c)` is os-backed (read+write of the local filesystem); `fileio.RegisterFS(c, fs.FS)` is sandboxed and omits `writefile` since `fs.FS` is read-only. Use the FS variant for untrusted SQL.
- **`lines`** — line-by-line text-file vtab. `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE log USING lines(filename='app.log')`, then `SELECT lineno, line FROM log WHERE line LIKE 'ERROR%'`. `lines.Register(c)` opens with `os.Open`; `lines.RegisterFS(c, fsys)` sandboxes.
- **`pivot`** — cross-tab vtab driven by three SELECT statements: row keys, column keys (value + display name), and a per-cell aggregate. `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE p USING pivot('SELECT DISTINCT region FROM sales', 'SELECT product, product FROM (SELECT DISTINCT product FROM sales)', 'SELECT SUM(units) FROM sales WHERE region=? AND product=?')`. The cell stmt is cached on the cursor, so a wide pivot doesn't re-prepare per cell.
- **`rtree`** — R-Tree spatial index. The `rtree` / `geopoly` vtabs are compiled in, so `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE demo USING rtree(id, minX, maxX, minY, maxY)` works unregistered. The typed `rtree.Table` hides that DDL and the overlap-predicate SQL: `Create(ctx, db, "venues", rtree.WithDimensions(2))`, `InsertPoint(ctx, id, x, y)` / `Insert(ctx, id, min0, max0, …)`, `Search(ctx, box…)` (bounding-box overlap, index-driven), `SearchCircle(ctx, cx, cy, r)`, `Delete`, `Drop`. Because the module is built in, only `SearchCircle` (the geometry) needs registration — `ext/rtree.Register(c)` adds the `circle(cx, cy, r)` geometry, or blank-import `ext/rtree/auto`. For arbitrary geometry call root `(*Conn).RegisterRTreeGeometry` (a Go bounding-box overlap test) or `(*Conn).RegisterRTreeQuery` (the second-generation query callback: classify each node not/partly/fully-within and assign a visit-order score). Unlike the ncruces `ext/rtree`, which loads a WASM module, this binds the transpiled C `sqlite3_rtree_geometry_callback` / `query_callback`.
- **`series`** — `generate_series(start, stop[, step])` table-valued function: `SELECT value FROM generate_series(1, 10, 2)`. start and stop required (the built-in treats stop as optional/unbounded; this port requires it to avoid a runaway scan), step defaults to 1 and may be negative for a descending series.
- **`regexp/gorm`** — `regexpgorm.WhereRegex(column, pattern)` returns a `clause.Expression` that combines GLOB prefix optimization with REGEXP. For anchored patterns this lets SQLite's planner do a range scan on the GLOB clause and treat the regex as a residual filter, delivering the documented LIKE-optimization win.
- **`regexp`** — `regexp_like`, `regexp_count`, `regexp_instr`, `regexp_substr`, `regexp_replace`, and the binary `REGEXP` operator over Go's `regexp` (RE2 syntax).
- **`spellfix1`** — fuzzy-text vtab. `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE vocab USING spellfix1`, `INSERT INTO vocab(word [, rank]) VALUES (?, ?)`, then `SELECT word, distance FROM vocab WHERE word MATCH ?` to retrieve the closest matches by Damerau-Levenshtein edit distance, grouped phonetically via Soundex. Persistent vocabulary in a `<vtab>_storage` shadow table; survives `db.Close()` / reconnect. Optional `WHERE scope = N` caps edit distance; `LIMIT N` caps result count. Go-native re-implementation of SQLite's spellfix1 (same SQL surface, simpler algorithm).
- **`statement`** — parametrized-view vtab. `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE adults USING statement('SELECT name FROM users WHERE age >= ?')` then `SELECT * FROM adults WHERE "?1" = 18`. Anonymous `?` binds become `"?N"` HIDDEN columns; named `:name` / `@name` / `$name` binds become same-named HIDDEN columns. Out-of-order constraints on anonymous params are remapped to their correct stmt positions.
- **`uuid`** — `uuid([ver, ns, data])`, `gen_random_uuid`, `uuid_str/blob/extract_*` over `github.com/google/uuid`. Covers v1/v3/v4/v5/v6/v7 (DCE Security v2 not implemented).
- **`hash`** — `md5`, `sha1`, `sha224`, `sha256`, `sha384`, `sha512`, `sha3`, `blake2s`, `blake2b`, `md4`, `ripemd160`. Each function registers only if the underlying `crypto.Hash` is `Available()`. Size variants (`sha256(x, 224)`, `sha3(x, 512)`, etc.) match nalgeon/sqlean.
- **`ipaddr`** — `ipcontains`, `ipoverlaps`, `ipfamily`, `iphost`, `ipmasklen`, `ipnetwork` over `net/netip`. Fixes the upstream `ipoverlaps` self-referential bug.
- **`zorder`** — `zorder(d1, …, dN)` / `unzorder(z, N, i)` Morton encoding for a tunable 2–24 dimensions.
- **`encode`** — `encode(data, format)` / `decode(text, format)` for base64 / base64url / base32 / base32hex / base16 (hex) / ascii85 (base85) / url. The codec half of sqlean `crypto`; the digest half is `ext/hash`.
- **`text`** — rune-aware string scalars SQLite lacks: `text_reverse`, `text_repeat(s, n)`, `text_lpad(s, n[, pad])`, `text_rpad`, `text_split(s, sep, n)` (1-based nth field). Casing/normalization stay in `ext/unicode`.
- **`stats`** — variance / stddev / skewness / kurtosis / covariance / correlation / regr_* / percentile / median / mode / every / some, all working as both aggregates and window functions (streaming Welford + Kahan + Terriberry). Plus `cbrt` and `cot` scalars.
- **`unicode`** — Unicode-aware `upper` / `lower` / `initcap` (with optional locale tag), `casefold`, `normalize` (NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD), `unaccent`. Preset collations `NOCASE_UNICODE` and `NOCASE_ACCENT` register automatically; `unicode.RegisterLocaleCollation(c, "sv", "SV")` installs language-tagged collations. The Unicode-aware `LIKE` override is gated on `unicode.RegisterLike = true` — default off, because overriding `LIKE` disables SQLite's LIKE optimization.

See `docs/coverage-ext.md` for the full matrix (status, upstream reference, test pin per extension) and `examples/ext-<name>/` for runnable demos.

## I want encryption at rest

```go
import "github.com/go-again/sqlite/vfs/crypto"

key := make([]byte, 32)             // derived from passphrase, keyring, HSM, etc.
name, fs, _ := crypto.New(crypto.Options{Key: key})
defer fs.Close()

db, _ := sql.Open("sqlite", "file:secret.db?vfs="+name)
```

Pure-Go page-level encryption — Adiantum default (32-byte key) or AES-XTS-256 (64-byte key, `crypto.Options{Cipher: crypto.AESXTS}`). The main DB, rollback journal, WAL frames, temp files, and sub-journals are all encrypted; the `-shm` WAL index stays plaintext (memory-mapped, not user data). Length-preserving on disk: zero overhead per page. No MAC, no SQLCipher format compatibility — confidentiality only; pair with disk-level integrity (LUKS dm-integrity, ZFS) if active tampering is in scope. Key management (derivation, rotation, storage) is the caller's responsibility — we treat the key bytes as opaque. For key rotation use the open-new-VFS, copy-rows, atomic-rename recipe documented in `vfs/crypto/doc.go` — the same pattern covers cipher rotation and migrating off a pre-format-break encrypted DB. For per-IO observability set `Options.Recorder` to a custom `crypto.Recorder` or use the built-in `crypto.NewSlogRecorder(slog.Default())`; the file kind (main_db / journal / wal / temp / sub_journal) is tagged on every event so metrics consumers can split by it.

## I want corruption detection at rest

```go
import "github.com/go-again/sqlite/vfs/cksm"

name, fs, _ := cksm.New(cksm.Options{})
defer fs.Close()

db, _ := sql.Open("sqlite", "file:journal.db?vfs="+name)
sc, _ := db.Conn(ctx)
sc.Raw(func(d any) error { return d.(*sqlite.Conn).EnableChecksums("main") })
```

Pure-Go page-level Fletcher-style checksum trailer (8 bytes per page). `(*sqlite.Conn).EnableChecksums("main")` sets reserved_bytes=8 on the schema and runs `VACUUM` to rewrite every existing page with a trailer. On subsequent opens the VFS detects byte 20 == 8 in the SQLite header and auto-activates verification; a corrupted page surfaces as `SQLITE_IOERR_DATA` on read. Both `cksm.Options` and `crypto.Options` accept a `WrapVFS` field for stacking — register cksm first, then point crypto at it for checksum-on-the-inside / encrypt-on-the-outside.

## I want fast in-memory tests with snapshot isolation

```go
import "github.com/go-again/sqlite/vfs/mvcc"

name, fs, _ := mvcc.New(mvcc.Options{})
defer fs.Close()

// Named SHARED DBs (multiple sql.Open handles see the same data):
db, _ := sql.Open("sqlite", "file:/shared.db?vfs="+name)

// PRIVATE DBs (each sql.Open gets its own independent store):
db2, _ := sql.Open("sqlite", "file:scratch.db?vfs="+name)
```

In-memory MVCC VFS — reader snapshots taken at SHARED-lock acquire; writer mutations buffered until xSync, then atomically published as a new snapshot. Concurrent readers see the pre-commit state for the duration of their transaction. One writer at a time per shared DB; private DBs are fully isolated. WAL mode is not supported (no log file in an in-memory store); use the snapshot-isolation semantics directly. Trade-offs: no durability, no checkpoint, per-commit memory copy is proportional to dataset size.

# Open shortcuts

For common configurations, skip building a DSN by hand:

- `sqlite.OpenInMemory()` — anonymous private in-memory DB
- `sqlite.OpenWAL(path)` — file-backed with WAL journal mode + NORMAL sync, the right default for write-heavy apps
- `sqlite.OpenReadOnly(path)` — read-only file open (no schema modifications, no journal)
- `sqlite.OpenShared(name)` — process-wide shared in-memory DB addressable by `name`

Each is a thin wrapper over `sql.Open(DriverName, …)` with the matching DSN baked in. Compose with `sqlite.Open(sqlite.Config{…})` when you need typed `Pragmas`, `Encryption`, or the full Config surface.

# Typed Pragma enums

`sqlite.Config{Pragmas: ...}` accepts typed enum values so you don't fight string-typos at runtime:

- `sqlite.JournalModeWAL` / `JournalModeMemory` / `JournalModeDelete` / `JournalModeTruncate` / `JournalModeOff` / `JournalModePersist`
- `sqlite.SyncOff` / `SyncNormal` / `SyncFull` / `SyncExtra`
- `sqlite.LockingModeNormal` / `LockingModeExclusive`
- `sqlite.TempStoreDefault` / `TempStoreFile` / `TempStoreMemory`

Each implements `Stringer` so it round-trips into the DSN form SQLite expects. Mix freely with raw string keys for less-common pragmas.

# Pitfalls

These bite at runtime and aren't obvious from the API surface. Read
this section.

## Bind values capped at 2 GiB

SQLite's `sqlite3_bind_text` / `sqlite3_bind_blob` use an int32 length field. Passing a string or `[]byte` larger than `math.MaxInt32` (2 GiB) now surfaces a clear error instead of silently truncating to a negative length (which SQLite interprets as "use strlen" or "until null", producing corrupted data). On 64-bit hosts this primarily matters for callers streaming whole large media blobs through `Exec(?)` — chunk them, or use `(*sqlite.Conn).OpenBlob` for incremental BLOB I/O.

## Virtual tables are per-connection

`vec0` (sqlite-vec) and FTS5 virtual tables are created on the SQLite
connection that ran the `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE` statement and are not
visible to other connections in the pool. If your code path can grab
any conn from `*sql.DB`'s pool, you'll see "no such table" errors.

Fix: either pin the pool to one conn for the lifetime of the DB
(`db.SetMaxOpenConns(1)`) or use a file-backed DSN with the virtual
tables persisted on disk so every fresh conn sees them via SQLite's
schema cache. The test fixtures in this repo pin to 1 conn because
they use `:memory:` databases.

## The libc version pin

`modernc.org/sqlite/lib` is transpiled C tightly coupled to a specific
`modernc.org/libc` version. **Bumping one without the other breaks the
generated ABI at runtime** with cryptic crashes.

If your project depends on this driver and you bump `modernc.org/sqlite`
manually, also align `modernc.org/libc` to whatever that sqlite release
pins. `go mod tidy` resolves the transitive set correctly when you
bump `modernc.org/sqlite`; the failure mode is bumping libc
*independently*, which `go mod tidy` won't catch.

Check the current pin:

```sh
go list -m modernc.org/libc
```

## Per-conn hooks need a pinned conn

`RegisterUpdateHook`, `RegisterAuthorizer`, `SetTrace`,
`RegisterPreUpdateHook` install state on **one** SQLite connection.
`db.Exec` / `db.Query` may pick any conn from the pool, so a hook
installed once and called via `db.*` is effectively random.

Idiom:

```go
db.SetMaxOpenConns(1)        // or use a single-conn session
sc, _ := db.Conn(ctx)
sc.Raw(func(dc any) error {
    c := dc.(*sqlite.Conn)
    c.RegisterUpdateHook(...)
    return nil
})
// Use sc.ExecContext from here on, NOT db.Exec.
```

## KNN inside a gorm.Transaction is not supported

`vec/gorm.KNN[T]` reads the sidecar through `*sql.DB`, not the active
`*sql.Tx`. Inside a `gorm.Transaction`, KNN won't see your tx's
uncommitted writes, and under a pinned-conn pool (the common SQLite
setup) it will **deadlock** waiting for the conn the parent tx is
holding.

Workarounds:
- Issue raw SQL through `tx.Raw(...)` against the sidecar (`<table>_vec`).
- Commit the parent tx first, then KNN.

`fts/gorm.Search` does route through the active pool, so it sees
read-your-own-writes inside a tx.

## sqlite-vec quirks

- `INSERT OR REPLACE` is **not** honored on `vec0`. Use `(*Table).Update`
  to overwrite a rowid, or delete-then-insert.
- The `vec0(...)` column-argument parser rejects quoted identifiers.
  We validate names via `vec.ValidIdent` before interpolation;
  table/column names you pass must match `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`.
- `LIMIT` is inlined as a literal in `KNN`'s generated SQL because
  sqlite-vec's planner needs it visible alongside the MATCH conjunct.
- Metric keywords are `l1` / `l2` / `cosine`. `vec.Dot` is an alias
  for L1, kept for historical naming.

## Soft-delete sidecars

When a vec/gorm model has `gorm.DeletedAt`, the sidecar gets an extra
`deleted INTEGER` metadata column. The plugin sets it to 0 on insert
and to 1 when gorm processes a soft-delete UPDATE. Default KNN filters
out rows with `deleted=1`. Pass `vecgorm.IncludeDeleted()` (and
typically `db.Unscoped()` for the materialization fetch) to query
across both.

For fts/gorm, external mode mirrors source's `deleted_at` as a
`deleted_at UNINDEXED` column; in-table / contentless modes use a
`deleted UNINDEXED` flag maintained by row callbacks.

## What's not supported

- **Userauth** (`_auth*` DSN flags): dropped upstream by modernc.
- **SQLCipher on-disk format**: we don't read or write SQLCipher's page
  layout (per-page IV + HMAC + KDF salt). Encryption at rest is
  available via `vfs/crypto` but it's a different on-disk format —
  see the "I want encryption at rest" recipe above.
- **`_mutex=no`**: modernc doesn't expose the unsafe single-threaded
  mode.

# Migration recipes

The driver is a drop-in for four upstream packages. Each migration is
a one-line import swap; the public API stays compatible.

## From mattn/go-sqlite3

```diff
-import _ "github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3"
+import _ "github.com/go-again/sqlite"
```

Driver name stays `"sqlite3"`. `&SQLiteDriver{Extensions, ConnectHook}`
still works (it's an alias for our `Driver`). `RegisterFunc`,
`RegisterAggregator`, `ConnectionHook` — all there.

Build tag changes: drop `-tags sqlite_userauth` (rejected) and
`-tags sqlite_vtable` (vtable is on by default). CGo flags
(`-tags=sqlite_fts5`, `-tags=sqlite_json1`) are unnecessary — FTS5 and
JSON1 are compiled in.

## From modernc.org/sqlite

```diff
-import _ "modernc.org/sqlite"
+import _ "github.com/go-again/sqlite"
```

Driver name stays `"sqlite"`. Public API stays the same. You gain the
per-conn hooks (`RegisterUpdateHook`, etc.) that modernc doesn't
expose; existing code keeps working.

## From glebarez/sqlite

```diff
-import "github.com/glebarez/sqlite"
+import sqlitegorm "github.com/go-again/sqlite/gorm"

-db, _ := gorm.Open(sqlite.Open("file:app.db"), &gorm.Config{})
+db, _ := gorm.Open(sqlitegorm.Open("file:app.db"), &gorm.Config{})
```

Same dialector behaviour. The driver underneath is no longer modernc
directly but this module's wrapper layer on top of it — the libc pin
invariant above applies.

## From gorm.io/driver/sqlite (mattn-based)

```diff
-import "gorm.io/driver/sqlite"
+import sqlitegorm "github.com/go-again/sqlite/gorm"

-db, _ := gorm.Open(sqlite.Open("file:app.db"), &gorm.Config{})
+db, _ := gorm.Open(sqlitegorm.Open("file:app.db"), &gorm.Config{})
```

Same swap. The mattn CGo dependency goes away.

# What NOT to do

- **Don't** call `vecgorm.KNN[T]` inside a `gorm.Transaction` (see
  pitfalls above). Use `tx.Raw` against the sidecar instead.
- **Don't** use `_auth*` DSN flags; they're rejected with a clear error.
- **Don't** bump `modernc.org/libc` independently of `modernc.org/sqlite`.
- **Don't** install per-conn hooks via `db.Exec` — pin a conn first.
- **Don't** expect `INSERT OR REPLACE` to work on `vec0` rows.
- **Don't** SELECT/UPDATE virtual tables across multiple conns of an
  unpinned `:memory:` pool.
- **Don't** rely on `Stmt.Exec` / `Stmt.Query` / `Conn.Begin` /
  `Conn.Exec` / `Conn.Query` — they're deprecated by `database/sql`'s
  contract. Use the `Context` variants. The driver implements both for
  compatibility, but new code should use the new names.

# Versioning and stability

Public API is settling but not frozen. Renames between development
tags are allowed (the most recent rename pass swapped `Match` →
`Neighbor`, `Item` → `Row`, `Result[T]` → `Hit[T]`, `WithWhere` →
`WithFilter` — without deprecated aliases, because the package was
fresh enough that no real-world consumers had to bridge). Pin to a
specific tag in your `go.mod`.
